questions.question: If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of the two adjacent angles so formed is:
questions.explanation: This is the Linear Pair Axiom: If a ray stands on a line, the sum of the two adjacent angles is 180°.

questions.question: The measure of an angle which is equal to its complement is:
questions.explanation: Let the angle be x. Its complement is 90-x. x = 90-x => 2x = 90 => x = 45°.

questions.question: If an angle is four times its supplement, then the measure of the angle is:
questions.explanation: Let the supplement be x. Then angle is 4x. x + 4x = 180 => 5x = 180 => x = 36°. Angle = 4 * 36 = 144°.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, the sum of the two acute angles is:
questions.explanation: By angle sum property, A + B + C = 180. If C = 90, then A + B = 180 - 90 = 90°.

questions.question: If one angle of a triangle is 100°, then the angle between the bisectors of the other two angles is:
An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one of its interior opposite angles is 30°. The other interior opposite angle is:
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = Sum of interior opposite angles. 110 = 30 + x => x = 80°.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. The largest angle of the triangle is:
Two lines which are parallel to the same line are _____ to each other.
questions.explanation: This is a theorem: Lines which are parallel to the same line are parallel to each other.

questions.question: A straight path joining two points on a plane is known as a:
questions.explanation: A line segment is the part of a line between two distinct end points.

questions.question: If two lines intersect each other, then the vertically opposite angles are always:
questions.explanation: When two lines intersect, the angles opposite to each other at the vertex are equal.
